title: Why Does Your Cat Knead You? 🐾
description:
Why do cats knead? Kneading, or making biscuits, starts when nursing kittens press their paws on their mother to get milk flowing, and many adult cats keep doing it when they feel safe and calm, while scent glands between their paw pads leave a smell that marks you as theirs.

topic: Why do cats knead with their paws?
script: Why does your cat knead you? It's a kitten trick it never quit. Newborn kittens can barely see, but they can push. They press tiny front paws into their mom, left, right, left, and that gets the milk flowing. Push, push, sip. Most cats just never outgrow it. Grown cats knead when they feel safe and calm, so a cat kneading your lap is kind of a big compliment. But there's a sneaky second job. Cats have scent glands between their paw pads. Every push leaves a smell you can't notice, but other cats can. It's like a tiny stamp that says, mine. Wild cats even knead soft grass to make a comfy bed before a nap. So when your cat kneads you, is it being a kitten again, or stamping you as its property?
key_facts: Nursing kittens knead their mother to stimulate milk flow (Live Science, PetMD)
Many adult cats knead when they feel safe and relaxed (Live Science, PetMD)
Cats have scent glands between their paw pads; kneading may mark territory (PetMD, VCA)
Wild cats knead soft grasses and bedding before resting (PetMD)
